children: CalciMedica reported a narrower quarterly loss than a year earlier, as lower research and development spending—primarily from reduced Auxora nonclinical activity and the pause of the AKI trial—more than offset higher general and administrative costs. A $3.3 million fair-value gain on financial instruments also improved other income.
² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Net loss per share - basic and diluted”.
: Research and development expenses fell 40% to $2.3 million, primarily reflecting lower Auxora nonclinical activity and the paused AKI trial.
: Expenses rose 38% to $2.4 million, mainly due to higher professional services and consultant costs.
: The company is preparing a potential Auxora Phase 2b trial after FDA alignment on trial design; initiation depends on additional financing.
: CalciMedica plans an Auxora Phase 1b proof-of-concept study, with trial details expected by year-end 2026 and data anticipated in mid-2027.
: Enrollment remains paused, and the company said it has no current plans to resume dosing as it prioritizes other development programs.
